Explore an aggregated tsibble through its series and dimension graphs

Source: R/grafts.R
grafts.Rd

Makes an explorer of an aggregated tsibble, drawn in the browser. The left column holds the series graph, drawn on demand, above the dimension graph of the key combinations given to fabletools::aggregate_key(). The right column plots the focused series, with forecasts when a fable is given, above a view of its children or of the pinned series.

Usage

grafts(
  data,
  measure = NULL,
  forecasts = NULL,
  level = c(80, 95),
  options = grafts_options()
)

Arguments

data

An aggregated tsibble, as produced by fabletools::aggregate_key().

measure

The measured variable shown first. Every numeric measured variable can be chosen in the app. Defaults to the first.

forecasts

A fable of forecasts for data, with the same keys (and optionally .model). Its response variable must be a measured variable of data. Each model's mean and intervals are drawn after the data.

level

Interval levels drawn for forecasts.

options

Which views the explorer offers, how it starts and is sized, and how its data are sent, from grafts_options().

Value

An explorer, of class grafts.

Details

Where the explorer goes decides how its series reach the browser:

  • Printed in the console, it opens in the viewer or a browser, served by a local server that sends each series when it is drawn, so data of any size can be explored. Like a Shiny app, the console waits while it is served: press Ctrl+C (or Esc in RStudio and Positron) to stop it. Use grafts_serve() to serve it in the background instead.

  • In R Markdown, Quarto, pkgdown or Shiny (renderGrafts()), and in a page written by grafts_save(), every series is written into the page, which needs no R session. This suits small data.

  • On a server, grafts_api() adds it to a plumber2 api and grafts_serve() runs it, sending each series when it is drawn.

Embedded explorers use the system's UI font. The served app brings its own copy of Source Sans 3, which a page can load too, for the same look.

Examples

tourism_agg <- fabletools::aggregate_key(
  tsibble::tourism, Purpose * (State / Region), Trips = sum(Trips)
)
tourism <- grafts(tourism_agg)

# Printing opens it, served from this R session
if (interactive()) tourism

# With forecasts, drawn after the data with their intervals
if (requireNamespace("fable", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(fable)
  tourism_fc <- tourism_agg |>
    model(snaive = SNAIVE(Trips)) |>
    forecast(h = "2 years")
  grafts(tourism_agg, forecasts = tourism_fc)
}
#> Loading required package: fabletools
#> <grafts explorer> 425 series of Purpose * (State / Region)
#> Measures: Trips (showing Trips)
#> Forecasts: snaive
